name: Amlodipine + Perindopril
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: The fixed combination is a substitution product for patients already controlled on the same doses given separately. Perindoprilat, the active ACE-inhibitor metabolite, is cleared by the kidneys and accumulates in kidney impairment, whereas amlodipine needs no kidney adjustment. The European label allows the combination only at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 60 mL/min or above; below that, the components are titrated separately. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min).
chip: Not suitable if CrCl <60: use components

bands.recommendation: One tablet once daily in the morning before a meal, at the strengths the patient already takes as separate drugs (SmPC). Monitor potassium and creatinine.
Not suitable at CrCl <60 mL/min: titrate perindopril and amlodipine separately (SmPC). Perindoprilat accumulates as kidney function falls.

hd.text: Not suitable (CrCl <60). Perindoprilat is dialyzable (dialysis clearance 70 mL/min); amlodipine is not. Use the separate drugs. Avoid high-flux polyacrylonitrile (AN69) membranes with ACE inhibitors (anaphylactoid reactions) (SmPC 4.3, 4.4).

pd.text: Not suitable (CrCl <60); use the separate drugs.

crrt.text: Not suitable; use separate drugs if needed. Extracorporeal circuits with negatively charged surfaces are contraindicated with ACE inhibitors (SmPC 4.3).

dialyzable: Perindoprilat: yes (dialysis clearance 70 mL/min). Amlodipine: no (about 97.5% protein-bound) (SmPC).
monitoring: Potassium and creatinine routinely in CKD; blood pressure, kidney function and potassium closely in patients at risk of hypotension or with renal artery stenosis. Hyperkalemia risk higher with CKD, age over 70, diabetes, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes (SmPC 4.4).
